## 📊 England v Senegal Form and Tactics
[...]
England drew widespread criticism for their performance against Andorra, despite the victory marking a significant achievement for Thomas Tuchel in becoming the first ever manager to win all three of their opening games in charge of the Three Lions to nil. This mini milestone was not enough to appease the press and demanding fan base who were brought back to Gareth Southgate’s tepid football on Saturday night.
[...]
Tuchel did acknowledge his side’s shortcomings in the game, claiming that he wasn’t happy with how his side ended the game. It’s clear that Tuchel was using the game as an opportunity to experiment, with Curtis Jones lining up as an inverted right back and Reece James tucking into the left-hand side of a back three when England had the ball. The attack took on an interesting structure as well, with Madueke, Rogers and Palmer playing in behind Kane. Madueke was the biggest success story from the game, but it would be surprising to see Tuchel return to this structure as it wasn’t effective, even against a side like Andorra.
[...]
Senegal have established themselves as one of the top sides in Africa over recent years and come into this friendly having not lost a game since 2023. Their defensive structure is particularly impressive. Across six games of qualifying for the World Cup, they’ve only conceded one goal, which may prove problematic for England given how much they struggled to put the ball in the back of the net against Andorra last time out.
[...]
Senegal’s main threat in an attacking sense to England is likely to be with their wide players. They have a lot of speed, which isn’t replicated in the England backline, which can help the visiting side catch out the Three Lions on the break. Ismaila Sarr, in particular, could prove a real headache with no obvious player in the England backline that can match him for speed.
